Singing was not a show put on for the church but something the church did together, to God and to one another, with heart and mind: 'I will sing with the spirit, and I will sing with the understanding also' (1 Corinthians 14:15).
entries.lesson: Sing with others, and mean it. Songs are one of the ways God's word dwells in us richly.

key_verses.text: Speaking to yourselves in psalms and hymns and spiritual songs, singing and making melody in your heart to the Lord;
Let the word of Christ dwell in you richly in all wisdom; teaching and admonishing one another in psalms and hymns and spiritual songs, singing with grace in your hearts to the Lord.
Is any among you afflicted? let him pray. Is any merry? let him sing psalms.

entries.name: The hymn of Christ's humility
entries.group: Songs of the church and of heaven
entries.epithet: He humbled himself, and became obedient unto death

by.name: Paul, perhaps quoting an early hymn

entries.occasion: Urging a divided church to have the mind of Christ
entries.where: A letter from prison to Philippi

lines: Who, being in the form of God, thought it not robbery to be equal with God:
But made himself of no reputation, and took upon him the form of a servant, and was made in the likeness of men:
And being found in fashion as a man, he humbled himself, and became obedient unto death, even the death of the cross.
Wherefore God also hath highly exalted him, and given him a name which is above every name:
That at the name of Jesus every knee should bow, of things in heaven, and things in earth, and things under the earth;
And that every tongue should confess that Jesus Christ is Lord, to the glory of God the Father.

entries.summary: Many scholars think these verses were an early Christian hymn: Christ came down from equality with God to death on a cross, and God raised him to the highest place.
entries.story: Paul was urging a quarrelling church to be humble: 'Let this mind be in you, which was also in Christ Jesus'. What follows has the rhythm of a song in two halves. Down: being in the form of God, he 'made himself of no reputation', took the form of a servant, and 'became obedient unto death, even the death of the cross.' Up: 'Wherefore God also hath highly exalted him', so that every knee should bow and every tongue confess 'that Jesus Christ is Lord, to the glory of God the Father.'
entries.meaning: About thirty years after the cross, Christians were singing that Jesus is Lord, and giving him the honour Isaiah kept for God alone: 'unto me every knee shall bow, every tongue shall swear' (Isaiah 45:23).
entries.lesson: The way up is down. Take the humble road Jesus took, and trust God with the lifting up.

key_verses.text: I have sworn by myself, the word is gone out of my mouth in righteousness, and shall not return, That unto me every knee shall bow, every tongue shall swear.

entries.name: Great is the mystery of godliness
entries.group: Songs of the church and of heaven
entries.epithet: God was manifest in the flesh

by.name: Paul, quoting what the church confessed

entries.occasion: Instructions for the church at Ephesus
entries.where: A letter to Timothy at Ephesus

lines: And without controversy great is the mystery of godliness: God was manifest in the flesh, justified in the Spirit, seen of angels, preached unto the Gentiles, believed on in the world, received up into glory.

entries.summary: In six short lines, probably from an early hymn or creed, Paul sums up the whole story of Christ from his coming to his ascension.
entries.story: Paul wrote so that Timothy would know how to behave 'in the house of God, which is the church of the living God, the pillar and ground of the truth.' Then he quotes what looks like a hymn: six short lines that end alike in Greek. God 'was manifest in the flesh, justified in the Spirit, seen of angels, preached unto the Gentiles, believed on in the world, received up into glory.'
entries.meaning: The early church put its faith into lines that could be sung and learned by heart. This mystery is not a puzzle but a secret now made known: God himself came in the flesh.
entries.lesson: Know the story of Jesus well enough to sing it. The heart of the faith fits in six lines.

key_verses.text: And the Word was made flesh, and dwelt among us, (and we beheld his glory, the glory as of the only begotten of the Father,) full of grace and truth.

entries.name: Holy, holy, holy
entries.group: Songs of the church and of heaven
entries.epithet: Lord God Almighty, which was, and is, and is to come

by.name: The four beasts and the twenty-four elders

entries.occasion: John's vision of the throne of God
entries.where: Heaven, in the vision John was given on Patmos

lines: And the four beasts had each of them six wings about him; and they were full of eyes within: and they rest not day and night, saying, Holy, holy, holy, Lord God Almighty, which was, and is, and is to come.
Thou art worthy, O Lord, to receive glory and honour and power: for thou hast created all things, and for thy pleasure they are and were created.

entries.summary: Around God's throne the living creatures never stop singing 'Holy, holy, holy', and the elders cast their crowns before the throne and worship the Creator.
entries.story: A door opened in heaven, and John saw a throne with a rainbow like an emerald around it. Four living creatures, full of eyes, 'rest not day and night, saying, Holy, holy, holy, Lord God Almighty, which was, and is, and is to come.' Each time they do, the twenty-four elders fall down, 'cast their crowns before the throne', and sing, 'Thou art worthy, O Lord, to receive glory and honour and power: for thou hast created all things'.
entries.meaning: Isaiah heard the seraphim sing the same words eight centuries earlier: 'Holy, holy, holy, is the LORD of hosts' (Isaiah 6:3). Reginald Heber's hymn “Holy, Holy, Holy! Lord God Almighty!” takes its words from here.
entries.lesson: Worship begins with who God is. Before we ask for anything, heaven reminds us that he is holy and worthy.

key_verses.text: And one cried unto another, and said, Holy, holy, holy, is the LORD of hosts: the whole earth is full of his glory.

entries.name: The new song of the Lamb
entries.group: Songs of the church and of heaven
entries.epithet: Worthy is the Lamb that was slain

by.name: The four beasts, the elders, and countless angels

entries.occasion: The Lamb takes the sealed book from the throne

lines: And they sung a new song, saying, Thou art worthy to take the book, and to open the seals thereof: for thou wast slain, and hast redeemed us to God by thy blood out of every kindred, and tongue, and people, and nation;
And hast made us unto our God kings and priests: and we shall reign on the earth.
Saying with a loud voice, Worthy is the Lamb that was slain to receive power, and riches, and wisdom, and strength, and honour, and glory, and blessing.

entries.summary: When no one could open God's sealed book, a Lamb that had been slain took it, and all heaven broke into a new song.
entries.story: John wept because no one was worthy to open the sealed book. An elder told him, 'Weep not: behold, the Lion of the tribe of Juda … hath prevailed'. John looked, and saw instead 'a Lamb as it had been slain'. When the Lamb took the book, 'they sung a new song, saying, Thou art worthy to take the book … for thou wast slain, and hast redeemed us to God by thy blood out of every kindred, and tongue, and people, and nation'. Then angels numbering 'ten thousand times ten thousand' joined in, and at last every creature in heaven, on earth, under the earth and in the sea.
entries.meaning: The song is new because the victory is new: a Lamb who conquered by being slain. It is sung for people from every nation and language. Handel's Messiah ends with its words, “Worthy is the Lamb”.
entries.lesson: Heaven's loudest song is about the cross, and every nation will be there to sing it.

key_verses.text: And every creature which is in heaven, and on the earth, and under the earth, and such as are in the sea, and all that are in them, heard I saying, Blessing, and honour, and glory, and power, be unto him that sitteth upon the throne, and unto the Lamb for ever and ever.

entries.name: The song of Moses and the Lamb
entries.group: Songs of the church and of heaven
entries.epithet: Great and marvellous are thy works

by.name: Those who had overcome the beast

entries.occasion: The victors standing on the sea of glass
entries.where: Heaven, beside a sea of glass mingled with fire

lines: And they sing the song of Moses the servant of God, and the song of the Lamb, saying, Great and marvellous are thy works, Lord God Almighty; just and true are thy ways, thou King of saints.
Who shall not fear thee, O Lord, and glorify thy name? for thou only art holy: for all nations shall come and worship before thee; for thy judgments are made manifest.

entries.summary: Beside a sea of glass mingled with fire, those who overcame sing a song that joins Moses' song at the Red Sea with the song of the Lamb.
entries.story: John saw 'as it were a sea of glass mingled with fire', and standing on it, holding the harps of God, those who had overcome the beast. As Israel once stood beside the Red Sea and sang, 'they sing the song of Moses the servant of God, and the song of the Lamb, saying, Great and marvellous are thy works, Lord God Almighty; just and true are thy ways, thou King of saints.'
entries.meaning: The Bible's first great song and one of its last are joined into one. Every rescue God ever made, from Egypt to the cross, is one story, and it ends with 'all nations shall come and worship before thee'.
entries.lesson: Your rescue belongs to a much bigger song. The God who parted the sea finishes what he starts.

key_verses.text: Who is like unto thee, O LORD, among the gods? who is like thee, glorious in holiness, fearful in praises, doing wonders?

entries.name: Alleluia
entries.group: Songs of the church and of heaven
entries.epithet: For the Lord God omnipotent reigneth

with.name: The twenty-four elders and the four beasts

entries.occasion: The fall of Babylon and the marriage supper of the Lamb

lines: And after these things I heard a great voice of much people in heaven, saying, Alleluia; Salvation, and glory, and honour, and power, unto the Lord our God:
And I heard as it were the voice of a great multitude, and as the voice of many waters, and as the voice of mighty thunderings, saying, Alleluia: for the Lord God omnipotent reigneth.
Let us be glad and rejoice, and give honour to him: for the marriage of the Lamb is come, and his wife hath made herself ready.

entries.summary: The only place in the New Testament where Alleluia is sung: a vast choir in heaven praises God because he reigns and the marriage of the Lamb has come.
entries.story: After the fall of Babylon, John heard 'a great voice of much people in heaven, saying, Alleluia; Salvation, and glory, and honour, and power, unto the Lord our God'. The elders and living creatures answered, 'Amen; Alleluia.' Then came a sound 'as the voice of many waters, and as the voice of mighty thunderings, saying, Alleluia: for the Lord God omnipotent reigneth.' And the reason for joy: 'the marriage of the Lamb is come, and his wife hath made herself ready.'
entries.meaning: Alleluia is the Greek spelling of the Hebrew Hallelujah, “Praise ye the LORD”, the word that closes the Psalms. Handel set these words in the Hallelujah Chorus. The Bible's story ends at a wedding, with singing.
entries.lesson: The last word belongs to God, and it is a song. Whatever happens now, the Lord God omnipotent reigns.

key_verses.text: And he saith unto me, Write, Blessed are they which are called unto the marriage supper of the Lamb. And he saith unto me, These are the true sayings of God.
